note: The node defines a := min_{1<=i<=m} n_i and asserts a <= n_i for every i, which is immediate from the definition of the minimum of a finite nonempty set of reals. The index set {1,...,m} is finite and, in the ambient context, nonempty, so the set {n_1,...,n_m} has a least element which is attained; being the least element, it is by definition <= every member, i.e. a <= n_i for all i. This is a definitional unfolding, not a substantive inference, and it requires no dependencies — consistent with the node citing none. No hypotheses about the p_i are invoked or needed here. The only degenerate case worth noting is m = 0, where the minimum would be undefined, but the enclosing statement fixes m >= 1 by supplying p_1,...,p_m summing to 1; the step is therefore sound as stated.
